thread_analysis.thread_summary: [COMPANY] works with [COMPANY] to assemble the compliance folder for a new Bluetooth registration, with the consultant offering practical flexibility on document fidelity (accepting a draft operation manual, a reused module block diagram, and simple scaled photos in place of formal drawings). After the compliance folder is delivered, the consultant explains the folder's retention requirement (one year after the registered product's end of sales, for presentation in the event of a Bluetooth SIG audit) and describes how future derivative models using the same module and host stack can be added to the existing registration's Product List for free via a simple self-service web operation.
all_questions_found: What is the status of the customer's preparation of the compliance folder documents (operation manual, product block diagram, product outline drawing)?
Can a draft operation manual (with specifications not yet finalized) be used for the compliance folder, on the understanding that it will be replaced later?
Can the module's own block diagram be substituted for a dedicated product block diagram if the customer doesn't have one yet?
Can simple scaled photographs of the actual product be used in place of a formal outline/dimensional drawing?
How long does the compliance folder need to be retained after registration, and what is it used for?
Has Bluetooth SIG ever actually audited one of the consultant's registration-support customers?
Can future derivative or expansion models that use the same module and host stack be added to this registration's existing Product List, and if so, how?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread illustrates practical flexibility in compliance folder document requirements -- a draft-level operation manual, a reused module block diagram (sourced from the module's own datasheet), and simple scaled photographs in place of formal engineering drawings can all be accepted, with replacement expected later for items still in draft form. It also covers the post-registration retention obligation for the compliance folder (one year after the registered product's end of sales, to be presented only if Bluetooth SIG conducts an audit) and the free, self-service mechanism for adding derivative models that share the same module and host stack to an existing registration's Product List via the My Page 'Manage Submitted Products' interface.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Compliance folder documents do not need to be in their final, polished form at submission time -- a draft operation manual, a substituted module block diagram, and simple scaled photographs are all acceptable substitutes when the customer's own finalized materials aren't yet available, as long as replacement is expected once finalized versions exist. The compliance folder itself must be retained for one year past the registered product's end of sales, specifically to be presented in the event of a Bluetooth SIG audit (an event with no track record in this consultant's prior client base). Once a registration exists, additional models sharing the same module and host stack can be added to its Product List for free through self-service web steps, rather than requiring a new registration.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Insisting on fully finalized compliance documents before proceeding could unnecessarily delay compliance folder delivery and registration closeout when acceptable substitutes (drafts, reused diagrams, simple photos) would suffice. Failing to retain the compliance folder for the required one-year post-end-of-sales period would leave the customer unable to respond to a Bluetooth SIG audit request. Treating a derivative model using the same module and host stack as requiring a brand-new registration, rather than a free Product List addition, would create unnecessary cost and registration overhead.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a customer's compliance folder materials aren't yet finalized, offer practical substitutes (draft documents, reused module-level diagrams, simple scaled photographs) rather than blocking on polished final versions, with replacement expected once finalized materials exist. After registration, make sure the customer understands the compliance folder's retention period and audit purpose, and proactively flag that derivative models sharing the same module and host stack can be added to the existing registration for free, rather than requiring a new registration each time.
